purpose: Test project sense granularity from contextual usage before independent expert review, while keeping source multiplicity, construction scope, joint applicability, unresolved ambiguity, and source-bounded coverage separate.

scope.source_boundary: For source-candidate reconstruction and coverage, use only the candidate inventory and its pinned OEWN 2025 snapshot. Contextual evidence enters only through the hash-bound train/dev usage pilot; it cannot add a source candidate or authorize use of STREUSLE test, baseline predictions, frequency, or an unpinned Web source.

usage_pilot.scope: 54 exposed STREUSLE train/dev occurrences across the same nine forms and 51 deterministic within-form round-1 pairs; STREUSLE test is excluded.
usage_pilot.ordering_rule: Complete blind usage-pair judgments and provisional usage clusters before commissioning final dictionary-to-project mapping review.

cluster_artifact.release_boundary: Publish only the frozen method, aggregate agreement, cluster membership by opaque occurrence ID, instability flags, and underdetermined forms; keep rater identities and raw work records outside the repository.

source_reconstruction.result: The 9 selected source entries and all 67 projected candidate records reproduce byte-for-byte; this is bounded source-route completeness, not completeness of English meanings or contextual adequacy.

interpretation: Sixty-seven unique source sense, synset, ILI, and definition identities establish source multiplicity, not 67 independently usable project meanings.
The VPC/VID candidate imbalance and purposive nine-form scope prohibit category-wide or population-wide claims about polysemy.
No context occurs in the inventory, so actual sense frequency, contextual ambiguity, joint applicability, abstention, and out-of-inventory rates are unobservable here.
Five definition-only candidates and zero usage labels require an evidence-sufficiency field; absence of a source example is not a rejection rule.
Exhaustive pairwise comparison would create 387 judgments per reviewer, so retained candidates are partitioned into proposed project-sense clusters instead.
Gloss similarity, shared words, source order, synset relations, or a model score may flag a question but cannot automatically merge, rank, admit, or reject a sense.

analysis_axes.question: Were any senses in the pinned source snapshot omitted?
Is the source sense equivalent, broader, narrower, overlapping, unrelated, or uncertain relative to the canonical form?
Does this meaning instantiate an in-scope lexicalized VPC/VID rather than a literal/free combination?
Which source senses should remain distinct or share one project sense?
Does one sense apply, do several jointly apply, or do alternatives remain unresolved?
How do exact-set, multi-label, ambiguity, abstention, and OOI results behave under one frozen inventory?

literature_basis.implication: Test sense granularity directly; reducing the number displayed is not a substitute for broader, usable distinctions.
Permit graded and jointly applicable meanings instead of assuming one categorical sense per occurrence.
Do not assume one crisp best sense or that one static clustering captures graded contextual applicability.
Keep contextual underspecification and simultaneous applicability distinct from annotator disagreement.
Preserve multi-label reference sets rather than forcing single-label WSD.
Use incremental usage-pair graphs to propose clusters without defining every sense in advance or exhausting all pairs.
Keep rule-based candidate generation, gloss/context filtering, occurrence identification, and inventory truth as separate stages.
Any coarse grouping must be an explicit, reviewable mapping, not silent deletion of fine-grained source senses.

roles.usage_rater_rule: Two trained raters judge the same frozen within-form usage pairs independently without dictionary glosses, source sense IDs, candidate counts, model scores, or each other's ratings.
roles.reviewer_rule: After the usage-pilot summary is frozen, two lexicographers who did not generate the candidate set review the same source inventory and provisional usage-cluster evidence independently and cannot see each other's decisions before both files are final.
roles.adjudicator_rule: A separately named adjudicator resolves disagreements only after both immutable pre-adjudication files and hashes are retained.
roles.developer_rule: System developers may prepare and validate files but cannot supply either independent lexical judgment.

derived_fields.rule: The template derives source_evidence from the frozen candidate record. Reviewers do not re-enter or override it.

cluster_rule.definition: A partition of every candidate marked retain. Singleton clusters preserve a distinct source sense; multi-candidate clusters propose one broader project sense.
cluster_rule.constraints: Each retained candidate appears exactly once; rejected or uncertain candidates never appear; members and clusters use canonical ID order.
cluster_rule.boundary: A proposed cluster is pre-adjudication evidence only and never rewrites, deletes, or admits a source or project sense. The public checker refuses to issue review templates until a later protocol version binds a frozen usage-cluster artifact.

workflow: Rebuild resources/polysemy_usage_pilot.json and verify the 54 exposed train/dev occurrences, 51 initial pairs, source hashes, and zero semantic judgments; do not use candidate count as project polysemy.

Collect two independent 1-4/cannot_decide ratings for the frozen round-1 usage pairs without exposing dictionary evidence. Add only prospectively frozen uncertainty or cluster-boundary edges within the per-form ceiling.

Create provisional usage clusters and a stability/under-determination report. The one-occurrence cut short slice remains insufficient for contextual separability and cannot be repaired by dictionary inference.

Only then run scripts/check_inventory_reviews.py --template separately for each lexicographer, set a pseudonymous reviewer_code and completion date, decide form relation and construction scope for every candidate, and propose a retained-candidate partition in light of the empirical clusters.
Store completed review files, reviewer-code keys, work agreements, and access logs in the approved managed location, not Git, GitHub Pages, an API response, or this Dropbox workspace.
After both reviews are final, run the checker on local paths. Retain the raw file hashes and the aggregate report before adjudication.
Adjudicate source coverage, candidate action, and clustering disagreements without rewriting either pre-adjudication file. Report actual inventory revisions only after adjudication.

After the inventory is provisionally coherent, run the separate occurrence-to-inventory pilot for assigned, multiple_assigned, ambiguous, abstained, out_of_inventory, and inventory_ineligible states; usage relatedness is not a substitute for this task.

public_fields: pre-adjudication file hashes without identity keys
privacy_and_release.free_text: No free-text field is collected by this protocol; rationales use fixed codes. Administrative identities remain separate.

acceptance.usage_manifest: The public manifest reproduces all 54 in-scope STREUSLE train/dev occurrences, 51 connected round-1 pairs, eight pairable forms, one insufficient-context form, and no source text or semantic judgment.
acceptance.usage_evidence: Every released pair has two independent judgments; added edges were frozen before rating; per-form disagreement, cannot_decide, cluster stability, and insufficient evidence are reported without forcing a partition.
acceptance.review_coverage: Both reviewers decide all 9 forms and all 67 candidates.
acceptance.independence: Both files affirm that the other review was not seen and prohibited signals were not used.
acceptance.agreement_report: Candidate relation, construction-scope, action, form source-coverage, and retained-candidate clustering agreement counts are produced without reviewer identifiers or raw decisions.
acceptance.context_boundary: No inventory review result is reported as contextual sense frequency, ambiguity, joint applicability, OOI, or WSD accuracy.
acceptance.completion_boundary: IR-136 remains incomplete until usage judgments and cluster diagnostics are frozen, two valid expert reviews and pre-adjudication hashes are preserved, adjudication is complete, and the actual inventory revision count exists.
